scope: Four official team transfers including same-person re-entry, five final provider credits, cumulative partial/full recovery, insufficiency, private events and real MySQL arbitration
applicable_agents_instructions: Explicit root/ancestor paths and backend subtree were searched; no existing applicable AGENTS.md was found.

contract.authority: Parent explicitly confirmed retaining the established merge-then-resplit rule; no new transfer-compensation rule was authorized.
contract.same_person_model: UNIQUE(order,provider) and UNIQUE(order,provider_account) retain one aggregate assignment per person. Re-entry adds the received pending share to the same original row. A later transfer splits that whole unapproved/uncredited aggregate.
contract.immutable_posted_money: Official transfers require IN_SERVICE and reject settled outgoing assignments or settled positive incoming assignments. Approvals require COMPLETED/PAID, so official approved or credited income cannot be rewritten by a later official transfer.
contract.source_audit: No required production defect found under this existing rule.

refund_assertions.mixed_sources: Historical C and current E release only their own fixture hold first; other original recipients retain same-order holds. Refund takes available or same-order remaining hold without touching the foreign five-provider holds.

all_five_individually_insufficient.method: Official penalty then reward around each serial failed refund; original successful order credits are preserved.

refund_assertions.failure_assertion: All rows and stored fields in the listed business/fund models are identical before and after each rejected refund. HTTP/admin audit rows and other unlisted models are not claimed to have no writes.

one_raw_boundary.oracle: Independent exact Fraction midpoint atom sorting, not the production allocation function

concurrency_cases.result: Both commits succeed, two active seats/five aggregate rows survive; exact final credits 700/2100/2250/1050/1400/2500 are asserted.

concurrency_cases.case: Same outgoing actor transferred concurrently to two fresh targets after re-entry
concurrency_cases.result: One success and one code 400; no orphan target assignment; four final provider credits plus platform settle/refund exactly once.

concurrency_cases.case: Same refund key over six original credits
concurrency_cases.result: Both requests return successful original result, only one OrderRefund commits.

concurrency_cases.case: Different keys with the same cumulative plan
concurrency_cases.result: One success and one 409; a fresh remaining refund clears every original exactly.

concurrency_cases.case: Released historical middle actor C income release versus partial refund
concurrency_cases.result: Only own remaining hold releases; stale plan is retried only after explicit new preview; other order holds remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

concurrency_cases.case: Five-recipient refund versus retained actor B withdrawal
concurrency_cases.result: Exactly one succeeds; withdrawal frozen money cannot fund refund; rejection/restoration allows fresh refund and full remainder.

limits: Assignment rows aggregate each person across pending service periods; individual same-person legs are not separate immutable earning slices under the established contract.

The dedicated late-transfer guard test uses fully approved/settled orders. Rejection of approved-but-unsettled COMPLETED orders was reviewed from the official IN_SERVICE entry guard rather than added as a separate dynamic case.
This new suite focuses on transfer/refund/holds/withdrawal/realtime. It does not repeat every historical gift, inviter, deposit-offset, coupon/VIP or crash-durability scenario.
Live local client integration and final live database auditing remain the parent task; this isolated runner never accesses xa_verify.
Six specified real MySQL concurrency cases passed; no claim is made that every possible interleaving has been proven.
